build_muscle.title: Muscle gain
build_muscle.calorieNote: A small calorie surplus — roughly +10–15% above maintenance.

macros.protein: 1.6–2.2 g protein per kg body weight
macros.carbs: 3–5 g carbs per kg body weight
macros.fat: 0.8–1 g fat per kg body weight

mealStructure: Protein at every meal (meat, fish, eggs, cottage cheese, legumes)
Carbs around your workout — before and after
Don't forget water: at least 30 ml per kg of body weight a day
tips: Keep the surplus moderate — a big excess of calories goes to fat, not muscle.
Protein is worth tracking precisely; carbs and fat can be eyeballed.
7–9 hours of sleep matters for muscle growth just as much as food does.

lose_weight.title: Weight loss
lose_weight.calorieNote: A moderate calorie deficit — roughly -15–20% below maintenance.

macros.protein: 1.8–2.4 g protein per kg body weight
macros.carbs: 2–3 g carbs per kg body weight
macros.fat: 0.6–0.8 g fat per kg body weight

mealStructure: 3–4 meals so you don't feel overly hungry
More vegetables and fibre — for fullness at a lower calorie count
tips: Too large a deficit slows your metabolism and costs you muscle — stick to a moderate pace.
Weigh yourself no more than once a week, at the same time of day.
Strength training on a deficit helps you keep muscle, not just lose fat.

improve_endurance.title: Endurance
improve_endurance.calorieNote: Calories at maintenance, with an emphasis on carbs for energy.

macros.protein: 1.4–1.8 g protein per kg body weight
macros.carbs: 5–7 g carbs per kg body weight
macros.fat: 0.8–1 g fat per kg body weight

mealStructure: Carbs 2–3 hours before a long cardio session
A recovery meal with protein and carbs within an hour after training
Steady hydration throughout the day, not just during the workout
tips: For long sessions (over an hour) you may need to fuel during the workout itself.
Electrolytes (sodium, potassium) matter with heavy sweating.

general_fitness.title: General fitness

macros.protein: 1.4–1.8 g protein per kg body weight
macros.carbs: 3–4 g carbs per kg body weight
macros.fat: 0.8–1 g fat per kg body weight

mealStructure: Balanced meals with protein, carbs, and vegetables
A regular eating schedule, without skipping meals
tips: For staying in shape, long-term consistency matters more than perfect calorie counting.
Food variety helps cover your micronutrient needs.

rehabilitation.title: Rehabilitation
rehabilitation.calorieNote: Calories at maintenance — we don't recommend a deficit while recovering.

macros.protein: 1.6–2 g protein per kg body weight (for tissue repair)
macros.carbs: 3–4 g carbs per kg body weight
macros.fat: 0.8–1 g fat per kg body weight

mealStructure: Omega-3 foods (fatty fish, flaxseed oil) — support recovery
tips: These are general guidelines, not medical advice — for injuries or specific conditions, consult a doctor or dietitian.
